transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Clarke (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Redwood Product); Anika Mehta (Cerulean Head of ML), Dr. Lukas Meyer (CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Security Lead), Aaron Cho (Infra), Marta Rossi (Privacy)

Summary:
Quick scoping call for a 6-week POC: focus on SOC 2/ISO check, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logging requirements, and running a throughput/latency benchmark on Dedicated capacity. Customer to provide workload samples; Redwood to propose test harness and security docs.

Topics: success criteria, target latencies, throughput, sequence lengths, batching, quantization tolerance, VPC/KMS, SSO/SAML, audit retention.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Anika (Cerulean): Hi all, Anika here — sorry we had a last-minute schedule shuffle, appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:10] Priya (Redwood SE): No problem. Priya here. I'm going to take notes on the benchmark side and outline the config.
[00:15] Dr. Lukas (Cerulean): Lukas here. We'll jump in on infra questions — we've got some tight constraints around data residency.
[00:20] Sofia (Cerulean Security): Sofia — security. I'll lead on SOC 2/ISO questions and KMS.
[00:25] Jordan: Great. Goal for today: align on POC success criteria, the workload sizing for the benchmark, and the main security asks for the pilot so we can scope Dedicated or Private deployment.
[01:10] Aaron (Cerulean): To be super clear, only PHI-ish metadata flows through the service, but payloads are pseudonymized. We still need SOC 2 and evidence of SAML SSO and RBAC so auditors are happy.
[01:35] Priya: Understood. We typically provide: SOC 2 attestation summary, ISO summary notes, a SAML integration guide, and details on RBAC groups and token scopes. For POC work, we can do Dedicated in eu-west and enable customer-managed KMS.
[02:12] Marta (Privacy): On KMS — can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer key rotation and BYOK?
[02:20] Priya: Yes, we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integrations. Rotation is supported but we'll need to document the rotation window and any cache re-encryption windows for model artifacts. I'll put that in the follow-up.
[03:05] Anika: Success criteria from our side: 1) p95 latency under 400ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens equivalent, 2) throughput >= 120 qps at 2-3ms per token average? (laughs) — rough numbers, we can refine, 3) audit logs that show request/response IDs and user attribution, retained for 90 days.
[03:45] Jordan: OK those are specific, good. Couple clarifications: when you say 512 tokens equivalent, is that average or max?
[03:58] Anika: Average is ~200 tokens, peaks to 512 for long-run analyses. So we need tail latency to behave.
[04:20] Priya: For bench planning, we'll want your distribution: percentiles of sequence lengths, concurrency, and what percent are embeddings vs generation. The Dedicated config we propose will be based on your 95th percentile sizes.
[05:00] Dr. Lukas: We can share a 50-req sample plus a synthetic load spec (CSV). Our infra team prefers rack-level isolation — at minimum network-level VPC peering and private subnets.
[05:28] Jordan: Noted. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering or Private deployments if you need on-prem. For the pilot we usually recommend Dedicated w/ VPC peering.
[06:00] Sofia: About audit logs — what fields are in the logs today? We need to show we capture requester identity, model/version, request id, timestamps, action type, and whether response included any PII flags.
[06:22] Priya: Our runtime emits: request_id, route, model_version, timestamp, duration_ms, user_id (if provided via token), and a redaction indicator when the classifier detects PII. For full enterprise we'll also enable action-level RBAC audit trails.
[06:58] Sofia: Who has access to those logs by default? We need RBAC so only certain groups can view de-identified content.
[07:12] Priya: We have admin, auditor, and operator roles out of the box. Access controls map to your SAML groups; we can also do attribute-based access if needed.
[07:45] Aaron: Networking question: peering vs private deployment — what hops are involved and do you accept strict egress rules from our subnets? We run restrictive ACLs.
[08:05] Jordan: For Dedicated we can set up private peering and NAT-less routes; if you need air-gapped we have an on-prem bundle but that's heavier. For the POC, peering with restricted egress should be fine — we'll provide a CIDR list.
[08:50] Anika: Bench specifics — we want to model typical RLHF-style endpoints: bursty traffic with 50 concurrent users, average sequence 200 tokens, top-k sampling in production. What hardware are you recommending?
[09:10] Priya: If your model is a 33B variant, for our Dedicated baseline we'd suggest 8x A100-80GB or a few T4s for quantized variants. If quantization to int8 is acceptable we can drop to cheaper SKUs.
[09:45] Dr. Lukas: We're evaluating both open 34B and a fine-tuned 13B version. Cost vs latency tradeoff — can Redwood run the same prompts on both and report unit cost delta?
[10:05] Priya: Yes, benchmark will include model A (34B FP16) and model B (13B int8), same prompt set. We'll report tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and cost per 1k tokens under our pricing model.
[10:40] Jordan: Also we'll capture cold-start vs warm-cache differences — we recommend a warm KV cache phase then the steady-state run.
[11:05] Sofia: For compliance, auditors ask for certificate copies — can you provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 summaries and scope documents?
[11:20] Jordan: Yes, we'll share the attestation PDFs and a short scope doc that explains what element of the platform is covered.
[11:45] Marta: Data residency/retention — we need logs to be stored in EU region and retention policy for 90 days, with export to our SIEM. Do you support log streaming?
[12:00] Priya: We support log streaming to customer SIEMs (Kafka/SQS/HTTPS) and can pin logs to eu-west storage. Retention settings are configurable for enterprise customers.
[12:30] Aaron: What's the support process if we see a drift in quality? We want alerts on prompt regression and rollback capability to a previous model revision.
[12:45] Ethan (CSM): We'll set up eval hooks — Redwood Optimize can run your eval set periodically and trigger regression alerts; rollbacks and canary policies are supported in the Console.
[13:10] Anika: On security — SSO. We need SAML 2.0 with group mapping, SCIM for user provisioning, and MFA enforced.
[13:25] Priya: We support SAML 2.0, group mapping, and SCIM provisioning. Enforced MFA is handled by your identity provider; we surface SSO auth logs and can restrict console access.
[13:50] Sofia: Are tokens short-lived? We prefer short-lived service tokens and rotation.
[14:00] Priya: Service tokens support rotation and TTL. For direct API keys we recommend short TTLs or using signed JWTs with your KMS.
[14:30] Jordan: Let's capture the POC timeline: Week 0: kickoff and paperwork; Week 1: test harness + sample data ingestion; Week 2: Dedicated environment provisioned; Week 3: warm-up and initial runs; Week 4: full benchmark; Week 5: security review + adjustments; Week 6: final review and acceptance. Does that map to your expectations?
[15:05] Dr. Lukas: Sounds reasonable — we may compress to 4 weeks if we can parallelize procurement and infra.
[15:30] Anika: Acceptance criteria again: 1) p95 < 400ms at typical load, 2) feature parity on audit logs + SSO + RBAC, 3) no data exfil detected in logs, 4) documented KMS BYOK flow.
[16:05] Priya: We'll enumerate those as pass/fail items in the report. For latency measurements we'll report warm and cold p95/p99 and show traffic shaping used.
[16:40] Aaron: For the bench, what tooling do you use? Locust? JMeter? Custom harness?
[16:50] Priya: We use a custom harness built on top of k6 and a lightweight recorder for your request traces. We'll publish the harness as a repo and you can run locally or let us run it in a dedicated cluster.
[17:25] Anika: We need to prove GDPR controls for the pilot: right to be forgotten flows and deletion of logs tied to a subject id. Can Redwood delete request logs on demand?
[17:40] Priya: Yes, we have support for targeted deletion by request ID or user identifier for enterprise customers; we'll document the pipeline and expected time to purge.
[18:05] Marta: Please note we require DPIA notes for model inference with special category data — any guidance?
[18:20] Jordan: We can provide a DPIA template and our privacy team will assist.
[18:45] Sofia: Off-the-record, do you have explicit attestations about not training models on customer data? That's a big ask for us.
[18:58] Jordan: Redwood does not use customer prompts to train public models; for hosted customers we can opt-out of telemetry ingestion. We'll include legal language in the pilot contract.
[19:25] Dr. Lukas: Network egress — will any telemetry cross borders? We need assurance logs and traces are EU-local.
[19:40] Priya: For Dedicated pinned to eu-west, telemetry and logs remain in region; we can use EU KMS. We'll confirm the data flows in the diagram.
[20:05] Anika: A couple of nitty-gritty bench numbers: can you capture tokenization time separately from model time and include KV cache hit/miss rates in the report?
[20:25] Priya: Yes, our profiler splits tokenization, model forward, and IO. KV cache hit/miss is tracked — we'll also surface effective tokens served from cache.
[21:00] Aaron: How do you handle model fallback if Dedicated capacity is saturated? We need graceful degradation policy — e.g., redirect to smaller model rather than dropping requests.
[21:15] Priya: Smart routing supports fallbacks to cheaper compatible variants and a throttling policy. We'll propose a fallback plan in the runbook.
[21:45] Jordan: On pricing — for the POC we can offer a capped spend estimate and bill monthly. We'll provide a sample cost sheet after we choose the two model configs.
[22:20] Anika: About logs — retention encryption at rest? We require AES-256 and HSM-backed keys ideally.
[22:35] Priya: Logs at rest are AES-256. We support HSM-backed KMS for key material — we'll note the process and any key import constraints.
[23:00] Sofia: For RBAC mapping via SAML groups, what's the granularity? Can we restrict by model route or only by console area?
[23:12] Priya: We support route-level policies and API-key-level scopes; mapping SAML groups to RBAC roles can be granular.
[23:40] Anika: Can you also provide an audit trail of admin actions (who changed rollout, who rotated keys)?
[23:50] Priya: Yes, admin audit logs are part of the enterprise offering; they include user id, action, timestamp, and previous/after state.
[24:15] Dr. Lukas: For benchmarks, we want reproducibility. Can you snapshot model and runtime config so we can reproduce results later?
[24:30] Priya: We'll produce a reproducible run artifact: model hash, runtime flags, kernel selections, quantization params, and environment variables.
[25:10] Jordan: Ok let's go through immediate asks: 1) Redwood to send SOC2 + ISO artifacts and a short security summary; 2) Priya to draft benchmark plan and baseline config; 3) Aaron to share sample request set and SAML metadata; 4) schedule the benchmark window (we suggested next Tue/Wed).
[25:45] Anika: We'll try for Wednesday. If procurement slows us we'll push.
[26:10] Marta: Small privacy ask — will you accept hashed user ids in logs rather than raw ids?
[26:20] Priya: Yes, we can accept a consistent pseudonymization hash when streaming logs.
[26:50] Aaron: One more: can you run a short spike to confirm cold-start on the 34B takes under 2s for token generation?
[27:05] Priya: We can run a cold-start microbench; we'll include both cold and warm numbers.
[27:30] Anika: If we pass all items, what's the path to production? We may require a dedicated contract and annual commitment.
[27:42] Jordan: After acceptance, we move to a Dedicated reservation contract or Private deployment depending on needs; Customer Success will run onboarding and we'll define SLA targets.
[28:10] Sofia: Can you confirm your incident response window for P0 security issues?
[28:20] Ethan (CSM): For enterprise, we offer 1-hour P0 response with an assigned on-call and post-incident review.
[28:40] Dr. Lukas: Ok. Any open questions from Redwood?
[28:50] Priya: Just to confirm the peak concurrency and token distribution for the synthetic load — is 50 concurrent users and 10% long-tail at 512 tokens accurate?
[29:05] Anika: Yes, that's correct. We'll provide the exact distribution in CSV.
[29:30] Jordan: Excellent. We'll follow up with the SOC docs and the benchmark plan. We'll also include the network CIDRs for peering.
[30:00] Anika: One more item — can you show us an example audit log entry with a redaction flag?
[30:12] Priya: I have a one-line example, I'll paste in the follow-up. Example: {request_id: abc123, user_id: user-xxx, model: redwood-34b-v1, timestamp: ..., redaction: true, duration_ms: 320} — transcript may garble braces, but you'll get the idea.
[30:45] Marta: Provide data processing addendum?
[30:50] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach DPA template.
[31:10] Aaron: For the benchmark harness, will you give us the repo access so we can run locally?
[31:20] Priya: Yes, we'll grant read access and a runbook. The harness will allow switching model targets and measuring per-component timings.
[31:50] Anika: Regarding telemetry, can you send the schema of events you emit?
[31:58] Priya: We'll share the telemetry schema.
[32:20] Dr. Lukas: Great. If we find a regression in quality between model A and B, do you allow us to pin traffic to a single model during rollouts?
[32:35] Priya: Absolutely, we support traffic pinning and percent-based rollouts with quick rollback.
[33:00] Jordan: Any other blockers?
[33:10] Sofia: A final one — we need to ensure the vendor contract includes a clause that prevents training on customer data.
[33:20] Jordan: We'll include legal language in the pilot agreement.
[33:45] Anika: Ok let's summarize next steps and owners.
[34:00] Jordan: Summary recap: Redwood to send SOC 2 + ISO PDFs, SAML guide, DPA and DPIA template; Priya to send benchmark plan and harness; Aaron to share SAML metadata + workload CSV; Customer to confirm benchmark window (aiming Wed next week).
[34:30] Anika: That works.
[34:50] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[35:05] Priya: I'll kick off the benchmark plan today and tag relevant people.
[35:20] Ethan: I'll be your primary touchpoint during the pilot for acceptance and any operational questions.
[35:40] Dr. Lukas: Thanks.
[35:50] Marta: Thanks all.
[36:00] Sofia: Bye.

Note: transcript contains some automated transcription artifacts and occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., "K V cake" for KV cache in one sentence).

End of transcript.
